x: George Durrant, writing from Catterick, says that the weather is rotten but doesn't mind that as he has been posted to the R.A.C. Has since been in hospital with pneumonia, but is now convalescent and hopes to do a bit of training soon.
The entry was small owing to the recent call-up of youth and a notable absentee was George Durrant, who was suddenly called for duty two days before the race.

The race was won by a very promising young runner, G. Durrant, who is a protege of Syd Jarlett's, and he made good use of his 1.45 start to work his way through the long markers and come home a good winner.
George Durrant, having convalesced at Halifax, is back with his unit at Catterick. He won the Inter-Squadron One and Three Miles.

George Durrant, back with the R.A.C. after his illness last year, reports very fit. Our sympathies are with George, as he had his home bombed during November.
Details are not known, meanwhile congratulations. George Durrant has been so busy in India that he hasn't been able to do any running. Informs us that he is now over Junior age.

George Durrant is now in Burma where he complains of the heat and flies. In spite of constant sweating he is "as fat as a pig." Is hoping for 28 days "Blighty" leave.
George Durrant writes in admiration of Burmese teak and temples, but not so keen on forcing his way through teak in the jungle from Imphal to Rangoon.

Eric Herbert and George Durrant both upset the team selectors by their forward running, but these things have happened before and no doubt will occur again.

Our lads had gradually been working their way through the field with Len Marchant always up with the leading bunch, and eventually Mike Heard was 11th with Jack Brown 13th and George Durrant 14th, which was a very good show on their part.

In the final check-up it was found that George Durrant had run exceptionally well to finish 15th. Frank Abberton ran exceptionally well to win such a gruelling race after having to battle all the way.
Bush deservedly won the handicap while George Durrant continued his improved form to gain second place with Eric Bishop beating his brother, Alan, for third prize.
Bob Taylor was second in the 1 mile, with Reg Bolam in fourth place, and Len Adams was second in the 2 miles run, with George Durrant in third place.
